2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 13.08.2020 at about 5.30 pm., the petitioner was riding the TVS Heavy Duty Moped bearing reg.No.KA-50-K- (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.3623/2021 3655 along with his mother Smt.Gangamma and his 4 y e a r s o n L o k e s h B a b u a s h i s p i l l i o n r i d e r s o n t h e l e f t s i d e o f Gudibande-Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations, all of a sudden came from back side and dashed against the petitioner's moped from behind.
Due to impact petitioner and his pillion riders were thrown out from the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Govt., General Hospital,
Gowribidanur wherein first aid was done, then he was shifted to Someshwara hospital, Gowribidanur wherein the petitioner was treated as inpatient and underwent wound debridement.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was Agriculturist, Sericulturist and doing milk vending work and earning (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.3623/2021 monthly Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to said accident, he lost his future income.
The Gowribidanur rural police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 in crime No.0207/2020 under Section 279, 337 and 304A of IPC.
The respondent No.2 being the RC owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court hence, placed exparte and respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal and filed its written statement.
4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts.
It has admitted the issuance of the policy in favour of the respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 has denied the involvement of the car bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-9275 in the alleged accident.

It (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.3623/2021 has denied the age,
occupation, income and amount spent by the petitioner.

Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the offending vehicle regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which Ramanjinappa vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127453556/
2 required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 13.08.2020 at about 5.30 pm., when he was riding the TVS Heavy Duty Moped bearing reg.No.KA-50-K-3655 along with his mother Smt.Gangamma and his 4 year son Lokesh Babu as his pillion riders on the left side of gudibande-Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate,
driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations, all of a sudden came from back side and (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.3623/2021 dashed against the petitioner's moped from behind.
Due to impact petitioner and his pillion riders were thrown out form the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries.
10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.
He also got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P.13 which are FIR, statement, mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, discharge summary , adhar card, medical bills statements.

11. On perusal of police documents which are marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P6 it is clear that the accident took place on 13-08-2020 at about 5.30 p.m., and Ex.P.1 - FIR in crime No.0207/2020 came to be registered on 13-08- 2020 i.e., on the same of accident at Gowribidanur Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 304A of IPC.
Ex.P.2 - complaint lodged by petitioner on 13-08-  (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.3623/2021 2020.

Ex.P.3 is the panchanama, Ex.P4 is the woud certificate, Ex.P5 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which describe the spot of accident as towards Gowribidanur, Gudibande road, D palya cross, near Lakkasandra gate and Ex.P.7 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report which shows the damages caused the vehicles which involved in the alleged accident I.e., motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-K-3655 and car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275.

Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet which has been filed against the driver of car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9275.
12.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent regarding negligence of driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275, the alleged accident occurred.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.3623/2021
not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 which belongs to the respondent No.2 and respondent No.1 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
let me discuss one by one:
a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering:

The petitioner has contended due to accident he has sustained grievous injury i.e., tenderness over left pelvic region, tenderness over left shoulder, tenderness over chest and abdomen, cLW over right side of forehead 3 x 1 x 1 cms, CLW over back of head 10 x 2 x 2 cms, tenderness and swelling of left leg.

In order to prove injuries caused to him, he has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.4 issued by General Hospital, Gauribidanur which reveals that petitioner had sustained fibula fracture left leg and left scapular body fracture and doctor has opined that injury No.2 and 7 are grievous in nature and remaining injuries are simple in nature.

Further, Petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N.
and got marked clinical report and X-ray marked at Ex.P.12 and Ex.P.13.
PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner.

Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.3623/2021 reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:

Petitioner has produced 19 medical bills for a sum of Rs.70,520/-
which are marked at Ex.P.9.
During cross examination of Pw.1, Respondent No.1 has not put any suggestion therefore, it has been considered that, those medical bills are genuine and correct.
Therefore it is just and reasonable to award Rs.70,520/- under the head medical expenses.
c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges:
PW.1 has deposed that, immediately after accident he took treatment as an inpatient at Someshwara hospital.
As per discharge summary marked at Ex.P.7 which discloses that, petitioner took treatment at Someshwara hospital from 13-08-2020 to 24-08-2020 i.e., for 12 days.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 12 days and by including conveyance, in all a sum of Rs.12,000/- is just (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.3623/2021 and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was doing Agriculture, Sericulture and milk vending work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.

So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.

Accordingly, the fixed notional income of the year Ramanjinappa vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127453556/
5 2020 at 14,500/- p.m., Petitioner may took 3 months rest and he may lost income for those rest periods.

sentences.text: Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.43,500/- (Rs.14,500/- x 3) towards loss of income during treatment period.
e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.

The petitioner has also examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. who working as Orthopaedic surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dntal Center, Bangalore as PW.2 who has stated in his affidavit that petitioner came on 17-3-2025 for assessment of disability and gave history of alleged accident he sustained fibula fracture of the left leg, left scapular body fracture.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner was treated at Someshwar hospital conservatively and discharged on 24- 08-2020.
The petitioner now complains of pain and weakness in the left shoulder, unable to lift weight sin the left arm and carry his routine work as before.
On examination the petitioner has restricted left shoulder movements with wasting of the left shoulder muscles.
X- ray of chest shows untied fracture.
PW.2 assessed disability of the left arm at 30% and to the wholebody at (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.3623/2021 10%.
During cross examination PW.2 has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and fractured bones are untied and petitioner has not underwent any surgery.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 8% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 - Aadhar card in order to prove his age.
As per said document, he was born on 1-6-1978 and as on date of accident he was aged about 42 years.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 42 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.3623/2021 multiplier is "14" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
14,500 x 12 x 14 x 8% = Rs.1,94,880/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.1,94,880/-
under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

15.
Regarding Liability:

The respondent No.1 has taken contention that, at the time of accident,
petitioner was riding his vehicle without holding valid and effective driving licence.
The petitioner has not produced the driving licence.
PW-1 during his cross-examination
clearly deposed that at the time of accident, he lost the driving licence, it is not denied by the respondent.
Hence, there is (SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.3623/2021 no reason to believe the defence of the respondent that at the time of accident, petitioner has not holding valid and effective driving licence.
16. Further the respondent No.1 has taken another defence that petitioner was riding the vehicle without observing the movements of the vehicles.
In this regard, perused the petition wherein submitted that car/offending vehicle came with high speed from his behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Further after investigation, IO has filed final report as per Ex-P6 in support of the petitioner.
PW-1 subjected to cross-examination wherein he clearly deposed that car came in a rash and negligent manner from behind and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, due to which accident occurred.

Further PW-1 clearly denied the suggestion Ramanjinappa vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127453556/
7 that due to his rash and negligent driving accident occurred.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has got examined RTO, Chikkaballapura as RW-1 who has stated in his (SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.3623/2021 evidence that car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 was having valid permit from 30-5-2019 to 29-5-2024.
RW-1 has produced Ex-R1-vehicle transaction history report.
Hence except the suggestion, respondent No.1 has not produced any documentary evidence to prove his defence.
Hence the defence of the respondent No.1 is not believable that due to the negligence of the petitioner, accident occurred.
17. Further respondent No.1 has taken defence that petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of alleged accident.
PW-1 subjected to cross examination wherein learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not put a single suggestion/question about the said defence.
Hence, mere defence taken in the written statement is not sufficient to prove the same in the absence of documentary evidence.

At this juncture, this tribunal relied upon the decision reported in - MFA No.3459/2021(MV-1) ( Sri.
Sadath Ali Khan Va. Sri. Noor Ahmed Sayeed and another) wherein it is held that - (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.3623/2021 " 26.

entities.text: Sadath Ali Khan Va. Sri. Noor Ahmed Sayeed and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, not wearing protective headgear does not negate the right to compensation.
Courts have consistently held that the compensation awarded should not be diluted solely because the injured party was not wearing protective headgear.
The principle of "just compensation" requires that while contributory negligence can be a factor in determining the amount of compensation, it should not result in an unjust reduction.
The compensation must be fair and reasonable, reflecting the actual losses and the nature of injuries sustained.

NC: 2024:KHC:28807-DB had come to the conclusion that the claimant cannot take shelter under the cited case laws as there is a violation of Section 129 of the Act in not wearing the helmet at the relevant time.
However, the contentious contention is taken by the Insurance Company that the claimant was not wearing the helmet.
But the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation.
Keeping in view of the scope of Section 129 of the Act and in a given peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the entire liability shall be fastened on respondent No.2-insurance company".

18. By considering the above said citation, at the (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.3623/2021 present case also,
not wearing protective headgear does not negate the right to compensation.
19. Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the R.C.Owner and the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
-: O R D E R :-
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
